                    ### Question
                    A 70-year-old man with 29,000 leukocytes / mm3, 180,000 platelets / mm3 and 15g / dL of hemoglobin in a routine analysis. During the examination no adenopathies or organomegalies were observed. In the extension of the peripheral blood numerous shadows of Gumprecht are detected. What is the most likely diagnosis ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Monoclonal gammopathy of uncertain significance.
opb. Viral infection
opc. Myelodysplastic syndrome
opd. Chronic lymphoid leukemia

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient is a 70-year-old man with leukocytosis (29,000 leukocytes/mm3) and the presence of Gumprecht shadows in peripheral blood, which are indicative of abnormal lymphocytes. The absence of adenopathies or organomegaly further supports a hematological disorder rather than an acute infection or other causes. The combination of high leukocyte count and Gumprecht shadows strongly suggests chronic lymphoid leukemia (CLL), as these findings are consistent with lymphocyte proliferation characteristic of this condition. Other options such as monoclonal gammopathy of uncertain significance, viral infection, and myelodysplastic syndrome do not align as closely with the presented clinical findings. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is chronic lymphoid leukemia.
